# Micro-test design: "next step" sentence in api-error-messages

Status: design only. Nothing has been run for this design.

## Question

Does replacing "Say what went wrong." with "Say what went wrong and the next step the caller can take." make agents
include a next step in the error message they write?

Failure type: the agents' output is missing an element they already produce (a message with no next step). A
sentence-level wording change is the right form, so this is a wording micro-test, not a pressure scenario.

## Arms

| Arm | SKILL.md text the rep sees |
|---|---|
| A (control) | Current skill, old sentence, unchanged |
| B (new) | Same skill, only that one sentence replaced |

The baseline already run (6 of 10 with no next step) is arm A for one setup. I don't know which model and setup
produced it. Unless the partner can confirm that, it is not reused. Arm A is rerun on both models below, so A and B
differ only in the sentence.

The skill is the whole context, not the sentence alone. The skill's example message has no next step and the skill
caps messages at 200 characters. Both compete with the new sentence, and the test should show whether they win.

## Models

Two models, chosen by me because none were specified: `claude-sonnet-5-5` and `claude-haiku-5-5`. Both arms run on both.
Say if you want a different pair.

## Reps

10 per arm per model, which is 40 reps. One fresh single-shot subagent per rep, with no reuse and no shared context.
There is no API key, so reps run as Claude Code subagents or `claude -p` calls, whichever lets me set the model and
turn off tools.

## Task prompt

The rep gets the skill text, then one task. Three tasks rotate so no single case decides the result. Each arm and model
gets the same rotation (reps 1-4 task 1, 5-7 task 2, 8-10 task 3):

1. A POST /payments request with `currency: "usd"` fails validation. Write the 400 message.
2. A GET /invoices/9913 finds nothing. The caller probably used a draft id. Write the 404 message.
3. A PUT /users/42 with a stale `If-Match` version conflicts. Write the 409 message.

The prompt says: "Write the `message` string for this error. Reply with only the JSON response body." It doesn't mention
next steps, and it doesn't say what is being tested.

## Isolation

- Each rep starts in a new empty directory outside every repository, with no tools.
- User-level settings, instruction files and memory are off.
- Probe first: run one pilot rep and ask what context it can see (instruction files, memory, tools, other sessions, the
  user's name). If anything shows up that I didn't plan, fix the setup before any scored rep. Probe reps are not scored.
- Keep `specs/` out of every rep's reach, including this file and the proposal. A rep that reads one is VOID and is rerun.
- Strip names, project details and the user's email from the prompts.

## Registered rules (commit this file before reading any reply)

Unit: one message string.

- Next step present: the message tells the caller a concrete action. That means a value to send, an endpoint to call or
  a header to change. Example: "send 'USD'", "list drafts at GET /drafts". Restating the rule alone ("must be an
  upper-case ISO 4217 code") does not count. I score this strict reading as the registered one. I also record the lenient
  reading, where a restated rule counts, and report both.
- Length: 200 characters or fewer.
- VOID: the rep read a forbidden file, used a tool, answered something other than a JSON body, or the probe showed leaked
  context. A void rep is rerun and not counted.

Per model, the new wording PASSES if:

1. Arm B has a next step in at least 8 of 10 messages (arm A baseline was 4 of 10 with one), AND
2. Arm B beats arm A by at least 4 messages, AND
3. Arm B has at most 1 message over 200 characters, with no more over-length messages than arm A plus 1.

The change PASSES overall only if both models pass. If one model passes and the other doesn't, the verdict is "binds one
model only", and no change ships on this evidence.

FAIL: any other result. A reply that shows a reading these rules didn't foresee keeps the registered verdict, and I
report the counts under both readings.

Variance: also record how many distinct shapes the arm B messages take (a next step, a rule only, a cause only). If the
five or more shapes are scattered, the wording isn't binding even if the count passes. Report that next to the verdict.

## Blind scoring

1. Each reply is saved as a sheet with a random id. The sheet holds only the message text, with no arm, model, task order
   or file name that shows the arm.
2. The id-to-arm map goes in a separate file that I don't open until every sheet has a grade.
3. I grade each sheet against the registered rules, reading every message myself. I don't use a keyword count, because
   quoted rules and template echoes look like next steps.
4. Unblind after the last grade, then count.

## Spend

Cap: $1.00 of the $1.50 left. Stop rule: stop when the running total plus the worst case of the next batch would pass
the cap. Batches are by model (20 reps each), and I record each batch's cost as I go. Run the probe first, then Sonnet,
then Haiku. If the first batch costs more than half the cap, stop and ask before the second.

## Outputs

- `specs/baseline/microtest-api-error-messages/`: the prompts, the sheets, the map and the grades, outside the skill
  directory so nothing ships with it.
- A short result note: counts per arm and model under both readings, the variance read and the verdict.
